newsitem.title: USA: White House hopes for budget pact "very shortly".
newsitem.headline: White House hopes for budget pact "very shortly".

text.p: The White House said Wednesday it hoped to wrap up details of a budget agreement with Republicans "very shortly," which would clear the way for congressional action before the Memorial Day recess.

"There are about, oh, seven or eight remaining issues that need to be addressed and our team is very hopeful that they'll be able to close the gaps that exist and flesh out the details of this agreement very shortly," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

President Clinton and congressional Republican leaders agreed May 2 on the framework of a spending and tax cut plan that would would balance the budget by 2002, and their aides have been thrashing out the details ever since.

Asked if Clinton and the Republican leaders would have to become personally involved to resolve key remaining differences between them, McCurry said: "It may get to that point. I don't think it's necessarily at that point yet."
